pitch: What sets apart companies that became lastingly great: humble leaders, the right people, discipline and perseverance.
br: researcher · good is the enemy of great
credit for success · own the failure
The right people on the bus
How to recognize the right person
A climate where truth is heard
passion · best in the world · economic engine
quiz: According to Collins, what is the main obstacle to greatness?
Lack of resources
Already being good
Competition
Regulation
The comfort of a satisfactory situation keeps you from seeking better.
What paradox characterizes the Level 5 leader?
Charisma and authoritarianism
Personal humility and professional will
Caution and slowness
Optimism and naivety
Immense ambition, but for the company, not for oneself.
What does the image of the window and the mirror mean?
Look out the window when failing and in the mirror when succeeding
Credit success to others (window) and own failures (mirror)
Watch the competition
Communicate internally and externally
Level 5 leaders do the opposite of self-centered leaders.
In what order did the great companies act?
Strategy first, then people
First the right people on the bus, then the direction
Technology first, then the market
Acquisitions first, then culture
With the right people you can change direction; with the wrong ones even the best strategy fails.
What does the Stockdale paradox describe?
Optimism as the key to success
Keeping faith in the final outcome while confronting the brutal facts
Financial prudence
Refusing all forecasts
Naive optimists lose heart; the mix of lucidity and confidence lets you hold on.
What are the three circles of the hedgehog concept?
Price, quality, lead time
What you are passionate about, what you can be the best at, what drives your economic engine
Customers, employees, shareholders
Past, present, future
The hedgehog concept lies at the intersection of the three.
What role does Collins give technology?
The trigger of transformation
An accelerator, chosen in line with the hedgehog concept
An irrelevant factor
A threat to avoid
No transition was triggered by technology, but it often accelerated it.
What does the flywheel represent?
One big strategic move
An accumulation of consistent pushes that eventually build momentum
A change program launched with fanfare
An annual reorganization
Greatness comes from repeated efforts in the same direction, not from a miracle moment.
